note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 56; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 36) on data/benches/rates.json: what sets a rate, timed by absorbance. Copper oxide dissolving in sulfuric acid in a stirred cuvette held at 25, 35 and 45 C, then at 35 C in half the acid; the time for its copper to read 0.050 is inversely as the rate.
title: Experiment: rates, the order and the activation energy

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: Half as strong an acid: how much slower will the oxide dissolve? Type the order you expect: 1 if half the acid halves the rate, 0 if it makes no difference. Then click "predict".
steps.why: The order in a reactant says how the rate follows its concentration: rate = k [acid]^n. Predicted first, it is kept as you made it.

steps.title: The cuvette in the holder at 25 C
steps.text: Pick up the cuvette of 1 M acid and click the spectrophotometer. Right-click the spectrophotometer and switch its cell holder on ("holder off": it starts at 25 C).
steps.why: A rate depends on the temperature: the cell holder keeps the cuvette at one, so each run is at a known temperature.

steps.title: Warming to 25 C
steps.text: Wait for the acid to come to the holder's temperature.

steps.title: The oxide in, stirred
steps.text: Pick up the copper oxide and right-click the cuvette; click "tip in the solid". Right-click the cuvette and click "stir".
steps.why: Stirred, the copper that leaves the oxide's surface reaches the beam at once. The grains are held up in the liquid too: watch the absorbance jump as they dim the beam.

steps.title: Stirred up
steps.text: Wait a few seconds while the stirrer lifts the grains.

steps.title: Blank, and the start
steps.text: Right-click the spectrophotometer, click "blank", then "+ A": the start.
steps.why: Blanked with the stirred suspension, what climbs after is the copper's alone. The rate is steady at the start: timed from here, the time to read 0.050 is as long as from the oxide going in would be.

steps.title: Until it reads 0.050
steps.text: Watch the absorbance climb as copper ions leave the oxide's surface. Speed the clock up if you like.

steps.title: Its end, and its temperature
steps.text: Right-click the spectrophotometer and click "+ A"; right-click the cuvette and click "+ T". Open the notebook and write how long it took (the time of this reading less the start's): the label "t" and the number, then "write". Close the notebook.
steps.why: The same change in the same volume: the rate is inversely as the time it took.

steps.text: Pick up the cuvette of 1 M acid and click the spectrophotometer. Right-click the spectrophotometer and click +5 twice: 35 C.
steps.why: The same oxide, the same acid, warmer: only the temperature differs.

steps.title: Blank, and the start

steps.why: Each run is timed from its own blank.

steps.why: Half the acid: if the rate goes as its square root, the time is longer by about 1.41.

report.label: the activation energy
report.why: In the notebook: x the cuvettes' temperatures as 1/K, y the column t as ln, fit: the slope is Ea / R, so Ea = slope x 8.314 J/(mol K). Each portion's grains are the same, so the oxide's surface is too; a hand tips within a few percent of all of it, and the grains' dimming falls a little as they dissolve, the same in every run.

report.label: the order in the acid
report.why: n = ln(t half / t at 35 C) / ln 2. The acid reacts at the oxide's surface, where its rate follows the square root of the acid's concentration: halving the acid slows it by 1.41, not 2.
